exams.syllabus: ABRSM Woodwind Practical Grades from 2026 (the 2022 lists may still be used until 31 December 2026). Lists read from the board's official syllabus PDF.
comps: 150 total: three pieces 30 each (90), scales and arpeggios 21, sight-reading 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in every component is not required). UK UCAS points for G6-8 (Pass/Merit/Distinction): G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30.

Three pieces, one from each of List A (faster, agile), List B (lyrical, expressive) and List C (varied styles/traditions); the repertoire lists are the same as for Performance Grades. Live piano accompaniment required unless the piece is a solo/study; recorded accompaniment not allowed. At G1-3 some or all pieces may use woodwind accompaniment: DUET pieces (play upper part), DUET/PIANO either. Up to two unaccompanied SOLO pieces may be played. Some grades (e.g. Descant G2, G4; Flute G2, G3, G4, G6, G8; Oboe G1, G4, G6, G8; Clarinet G7; Bassoon G3; Sax G1, G2, G4) require at least one accompanied piece. Listed arrangement/transcription editions must be used; otherwise any edition. Repeats generally not played except short ones; da capo/dal segno followed; cadenzas omitted. May play from memory (examiner needs a copy). Related-instrument options: Descant may play one piece on tenor or treble recorder (then A/B/C lists still apply); Treble G1-5 may play one piece on descant, G6-8 on another recorder where indicated; Saxophones may play one piece (any list) on another saxophone; Flute G8 one piece on alto flute and Oboe G8 one on cor anglais where indicated. Pieces from the 2022 syllabus allowed until 31 Dec 2026 (all requirements from the same syllabus).

Practical Grades are face-to-face exams; ABRSM also offers Performance Grades (separate qualifications focusing on a whole performance) using the same repertoire lists, and digital exams; marks cannot be transferred between Practical and Performance Grades, and using different pieces for both is recommended. Alternative tests exist for specific needs (blind/partially sighted: Braille memory or aural repetition for sight-reading; deaf/hearing-impaired: alternative aural tests).
sections: Scales & technical work
Scales: F, G maj; A min (nat/harm/mel) - 1 oct | Arpeggios: F, G maj; A min - 1 oct | Articulation: tongued/slurred (examiner's choice)
Sight-reading
4 bars; 4/4, 3/4; dotted minims to paired quavers and rests; tongued notes or simple two-note slurs; dynamics (recorders mf only; others f and mf); keys (majors; minors): G, F
Aural & other tests
Clap pulse and say 2 or 3 time; sing back 3 two-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); spot a pitch change (near start/end); answer questions on dynamics and articulation of a piece

exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 4/5); Ofqual qualification no. 600/0949/4
comps: None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.

Official ATCL repertoire list for clarinet, read from the Trinity PDF (41 entries). Repertoire for A clarinet may be offered on a B♭ clarinet if the piano part is transposed; only one piece may be performed on an E♭ or bass clarinet. Programmes must consist of a minimum of two works, performed complete except where single movements are specified; programmes including own-choice pieces must be pre-approved. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.

p0019.d: Bacewicz's unaccompanied Polish Caprice: a brilliant, folk-flavoured miniature built on Polish dance rhythms, with chords, rapid passagework and a strong rhythmic drive.
p0019.rw: Brilliant solo showpiece; great for confident players

p0214.d: A tender, song-like miniature in Edwardian salon style, with a long, arching melody and warm harmonies. Tests sustained tone and expressive shaping.

p0662.d: An arrangement of Piazzolla's famous tango: insistent, driving rhythms and a sultry, aching melody. Instantly recognisable and energetic.

p0675.d: Poulenc's much-loved flute sonata (1957): a wistful, songful first movement, a haunting Cantilena and a sparkling, cheeky Presto finale.
p0675.rw: Much-loved French sonata; strong recital centrepiece

p0775.d: Three short, linked character pieces moving from dreamy and tender to warm, then to a fiery, driving finale. Originally for clarinet; needs rich tone and sustained Romantic phrasing.

p0675|Cello.d: Poulenc's Cello Sonata (1940–48), a larger four-movement work: a march-like opening, a tender Cavatine, a playful Ballabile and a dramatic finale.
